blockingIssues.description: The new `createMockProjectDb()` harness turns the claimed durable-store coverage into an in-memory simulation. Because `execute()` is stubbed to always return `{ rows: [] }` and only a narrow `insert/select` subset is implemented before `DbProjectStore` is constructed, the tests never exercise the real durable Neon/Drizzle path, table setup, or query execution semantics that this feature was supposed to verify.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Either provide the `scrutiny-feature-reviewer` subagent referenced by the skill or document an approved fallback reviewer droid so scrutiny runs do not fail at the reviewer-spawn step in environments where that subagent is unavailable.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: This scrutiny run attempted to spawn `scrutiny-feature-reviewer` exactly as the active skill requires, but the Task tool reported `Droid configuration not found for subagent: scrutiny-feature-reviewer`. The run had to fall back to the available `verification-auditor` droid to complete review coverage.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: When a feature claims durable-store or database-backed parity coverage, require proof against a real durable backend (or an explicitly documented limitation) instead of accepting Drizzle AST or in-memory fakes as durable-path verification.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The failed review for `durable-project-scope-db-regression-followup` found that its new `DbProjectStore` regressions use `createMockProjectDb()` plus query-chunk parsing helpers in `services/auth-broker/tests/project-admin.test.ts:89-192`, so the claimed durable-path coverage never exercises the real durable backend.
